chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman secretly from her family, while she was in her family's house, and he intended to divorce her but could not reach her to know her menstruation when she menstruates, nor her purity when she is pure. He said, 'This is like the one absent from his family; he divorces her with the new moons and witnesses.' I said, 'What if he reaches her at times and does not reach her at other times, so he knows her condition? How should he divorce her?' He said, 'If a month passes during which he does not reach her, he divorces her when he looks at the first day of the next month with witnesses, and he writes the month in which he divorces her, and he testifies upon her divorce with two men. If three months pass, then she is separated from him, and he is a suitor among the suitors, and upon him is her maintenance during those three months in which she observes the waiting period.'
The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: And the pregnant woman whose pregnancy is clear is also divorced once, at any time the divorcer wishes.

key_terms.غُرَّةُ الشَّهْرِ: The first day of the month

ai.seo_question: How does a husband divorce his wife if he cannot observe her menstrual cycle due to separation?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the fiqh of *Talaq al-Mu'allaq* (conditional or deferred divorce) for separated couples, emphasizing the Shia emphasis on precise chronological tracking (*Iddah*) when direct observation of menstruation is impossible. It distinguishes between total absence, where divorce is tied to lunar months, and intermittent absence, requiring a full month of non-visit to establish the start of the waiting period, while also clarifying that pregnancy overrides menstrual counting. This ruling underscores the scholarly principle that the husband bears the financial responsibility (*Nafaqah*) during this transitional period, ensuring the wife's rights are protected until the finalization of the divorce.
